# Orbital shells, integral kernels and the geometric trace

Chapter 1, §§1.1–1.3 and 1.5–1.8, introduces the Tate, Schauder, orbit and trace constructions and compares them with Connes and Deninger. §§1.6–1.8 include historical material and a second account of the method. The substantive matches for these sections are indexed by their later mathematical statements. §§1.4 and 1.8 also contain a concrete limiting argument, assessed separately in the endgame report.

**Port checks.** Physlib is Apache-2.0 and uses precisely the project’s Lean 4.36.0 and Mathlib commit. Eight trace modules compiled unchanged in a scratch directory. All three Physlib theorems above and the two named Mathlib measure theorems printed only `propext`, `Classical.choice` and `Quot.sound`. The Anthropic L²-kernel file (Apache-2.0, Lean 4.33.1) contains proof bodies and upstream axiom guards, but failed on this pin in the measure-theory proofs, including the `MemLp` constructor steps. It needs porting. The Hilbert–Schmidt norm proof in subfish-zhou (Lean 4.35.0) has a proof body with no direct hole. I found no license in the repository tree or README and did not audit its imported proofs. Use it as a proof reference only. An independent non-Lean source for operator ideals and compact-operator spectral theory is [Unruh’s Isabelle/HOL AFP entry](https://isa-afp.org/entries/Hilbert_Space_Tensor_Product.html).

**Additional search checks.** De Frutos-Fernández already proved surjectivity of the idele-class map to the ideal class group in Lean 3.42.1, Apache-2.0. Use `C_K.map_to_class_group.surjective` as a historical proof reference for A.1 if necessary. [Original Lean source](https://github.com/mariainesdff/ideles-journal/blob/fe49f5246910592f8ac56c5470b34f2c66a23220/src/ideles_number_field.lean) · [ITP paper](https://drops.dagstuhl.de/entities/document/10.4230/LIPIcs.ITP.2022.14). Two superficially close hits illustrate why proof bodies matter. Google's formal-conjectures (Apache-2.0, Lean 4.33.1) states `RiemannHypothesis.weil_positivity_criterion` with a direct `sorry`. In Riemann-adelic the declarations `weil_identity_Xi` and `spectrum_equals_zero_imaginaries` are axioms. Masullo §1.4.6 in any case takes a different route to the zero-location conclusion.
